newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes final pre-Christmas session up.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes final pre-Christmas session up.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index closed off the last pre-Christmas session with a small rise helped by a late rebound from major issues.
The PX50 rose 1.3 points to 531.1. The bourse will be closed until Friday for the Christmas break.
Dealers said the market, as expected, was very quiet although there was some activity in investment funds.
"I've seen some activity in the funds...but nothing major. Today is very quiet. Basically most of the traders are already on holiday," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings in Prague.

SPIF Cesky, which has attracted huge interest in recent weeks after management said it would seek to make the fund open ended, was the most heavily traded share in continuous trading, accounting for 5.5 million of the session's 18.2 milion turnover.

SPIF, though, was unchanged on 428 crowns per share. RIF investment fund, which also attracted strong activity, rose 11 crowns to 850. The major issues pushed ahead later in the day with Komercni Banka rising 20 crowns to 2,200. SPT Telecom gained 15 crowns to 3,310.
